analysis:
Speaking from the Red Fort on 15 August 2023, Modi said India had risen from the 10th largest to the 5th largest economy in the world.

World Bank GDP (current US$) data show India at about US$1.86 trillion in 2013, behind the United States, China, Japan, Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Brazil, Russia and Italy, and at about US$3.76 trillion in 2024, ahead of the United Kingdom (US$3.70 trillion) and fifth overall.

The ranking is sensitive to exchange rates and to the year chosen, but on the World Bank series both the direction of change and the fifth-place position in 2024 are consistent with the statement.
notes: The World Bank API data were read directly, which supports the verdict. quote_english is the PIB summary wording, so quote_is_verbatim=false. Rankings use World Bank nominal GDP (current US$); some outlets using IMF data describe India as 4th largest from 2025 after overtaking Japan, which does not contradict the 2023 statement.
